newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't announces fuel price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't announces fuel price hikes.

text.p: The Brazilian government announced price hikes for gasoline, diesel and alcohol used as automotive fuel as a result of cuts in subsidies, a scaling back of price controls and higher costs.
Government officials said the increases, which come into effect Dec. 17, would add less than half a percentage point to inflation in December.

The government was expanding areas where gasoline and alcohol prices are no longer subject to price controls to cover about 98 percent of the country, Bolivar Rocha, the Finance Minstry's Economic Monitoring Secretary, said.
That decision, plus the ending of transportation subsidies, would result in increases of between eight and 10 percent in the price of gasoline and alcohol, he said.
Diesel prices would remain under government control but would rise by between 8.83 and 18 percent, varying from region to region.
